claims.explanation: HSP90 inhibition by NVP-AUY922 is selectively toxic to cancer cells that depend on HSP90 client proteins for survival, particularly those with activated oncogenic kinases such as mutant EGFR, BRAF, NRAS, or PIK3CA, or with loss of PTEN leading to PI3K/AKT dependence. Conversely, cells with intact tumor suppressor pathways or low expression of HSP90 clients may be less affected. The pattern of sensitive lines enriched for TP53 mutations and oncogenic drivers suggests that HSP90 addiction, driven by client oncoprotein expression, underlies selectivity.

features.basis: Mutant EGFR is an HSP90 client; sensitive lines include NCIH1650 and KYSE270 with EGFR mutations.
Mutant BRAF is an HSP90 client; sensitive lines include HEC265, LOXIMVI, UACC62 with BRAF mutations.
Mutant NRAS is an HSP90 client; sensitive lines include IPC298 and KU1919 with NRAS mutations.
Mutant PIK3CA drives PI3K/AKT signaling dependent on HSP90; sensitive lines include SNU840, HGC27, MKN1, KYSE510.
PTEN loss hyperactivates PI3K/AKT, increasing HSP90 dependence; sensitive lines include 786O, HEC265, ZR751, UACC62.
TP53 mutations are highly enriched in sensitive lines, possibly reflecting genomic instability and HSP90 addiction.
Higher expression of the drug target HSP90AA1 may increase sensitivity to its inhibitor.
Higher expression of the drug target HSP90AB1 may increase sensitivity to its inhibitor.
High HSP70 (HSPA1A) expression can compensate for HSP90 inhibition and protect cells.
High HSP70 (HSPA1B) expression can compensate for HSP90 inhibition and protect cells.
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK signaling, which relies on HSP90; sensitive lines include S117, LOXIMVI, BICR6.
ARID1A mutations are enriched in sensitive lines, possibly linking chromatin remodeling defects to HSP90 dependence.
